label: L-K
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{L-K}
Given a nondegenerate lattice $S$, the map sending $M\supset S$ to
the kernel $K=L/S\subset\operatorname{discr} S$ establishes a one-to-one correspondence
between the set of isomorphism classes of finite index extensions of $S$
and the set of $b$-isotropic subgroups of $\operatorname{discr} S$.  Under this
correspondence, one has
$$
\operatorname{discr} L \cong K^{\perp}/K
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
L = \{\,x\in S^{\vee} \mid x\bmod S \in K\,\}.
$$

name: Nikulin

label: thm:Nikulin.genus
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Nikulin.genus}
	A primitive isometry $\iota \colon S \to L$ (where $L$ is a representative of a
	given unimodular genus) gives rise to a bijective anti-isometry 
$$
	\psi \colon \operatorname{discr} S \;\longrightarrow\; \operatorname{discr} S^{\perp}.
$$
	As a consequence, the genus $\operatorname{genus}(S^{\perp})$ is 
	independent of the choice of~$\iota$ and depends only on~$S$.
	The $G$-equivalence classes of primitive isometries 
	$\iota \colon S \hookrightarrow L$ are in canonical bijection with the following data:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item a lattice (isomorphism class) 
		$T \in \operatorname{genus}(S^{\perp})$, and
		\item a $G$-equivalence class of anti-isometries 
		$\psi \colon \operatorname{discr} S \to \operatorname{discr} T$.
	\@ifnextchar*\expandafter\@ifnextchar*\expandafter\@ifnextchar*\expandafter\@ifnextchar*\expandafter\end\expandafter{\@currenvir}\expandafter{\@currenvir}\expandafter{\@currenvir}\expandafter{\@currenvir}{enumerate}

label: arithmatical.reduction
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{arithmatical.reduction}
	Equisingular deformation classes of projective models of K3-surfaces of a
	given kind are in canonical bijection with oriented isomorphism classes of
	abstract homological types of the same kind.  
	A class is real if and only if its homological type admits an
	orientation-reversing automorphism $\tau$; it contains a real model if and
	only if $\tau$ can be chosen involutive.

body_md:
\label{sextics.norealrep}
	There exist exactly two disconnected real strata with $\mu \leqslant 18$, namely
	\[
	\mathcal{M}_{1}(2\mathbf{A}_{9}) \quad\text{and}\quad \mathcal{M}_{2}(2\mathbf{A}_{9}),

label: norealcurves
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{norealcurves}
	The stratum $\mathcal{M}_{1}(\mathbf{A}_{7}\oplus \mathbf{A}_{6}\oplus\mathbf{A}_{5})$ is connected and
	real but contains no real curves.  
	It is the only plane sextic stratum with this property.
head: environment
name: Akyol--Degtyarev, 2016

title: Theorem
body_md:
A set of singularities $S$ is realized by a non-special quartic surface if
	and only if it can be obtained by a formal perturbation of one of the 78
	extremal sets (59 maximizing with $\mu=19$ and 19 with $\mu=18$).  
	The strata
$$
	\mathcal{M}_{1}(\mathbf{D}_{6}\oplus 2\mathbf{A}_{6}),\ 
	\mathcal{M}_{1}(\mathbf{D}_{5}\oplus 2\mathbf{A}_{6}\oplus \mathbf{A}_{1}),\ 
	\mathcal{M}_{1}(3\mathbf{A}_{6}),\ 
	\mathcal{M}_{1}(2\mathbf{A}_{6}\oplus 2\mathbf{A}_{3})
$$
	split into pairs of complex conjugate components; the remaining
	non-maximizing strata are connected.
head: environment
name: G\"{u}ne\c{s} Akta\c{s}, 2017

label: norealsurfaces
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{norealsurfaces}
	There exist exactly two equisingular strata of simple quartics which are
	connected and real but contain no real quartic surfaces:
	\[
	\mathcal{M}_{1}(\mathbf{A}_{7}\oplus \mathbf{A}_{6}\oplus \mathbf{A}_{3}\oplus \mathbf{A}_{2}),\qquad
	\mathcal{M}_{1}(\mathbf{D}_{7}\oplus \mathbf{A}_{6}\oplus \mathbf{A}_{3}\oplus \mathbf{A}_{2}).
